amendments.because: The JSON now states its GitHub cache contract instead of promising identical output to a fresh read

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Both JSON views call `story.plan_ref` for finished story rows (`board.py:282,596`). When a retained local story branch and its remote have different tips, this condition starts `git merge-base` once per finished story, even though the story is done. Adding such finished stories therefore adds git calls. Separately, if a cached GitHub refresh fails, `nextstep.py:202-204` immediately makes fresh PR-list calls outside the board cache.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The finished-item proof writes story state and plans directly to the default branch and creates only fix branches (`finish`, lines 27-33). Its active-item case creates story branches, but never finishes them. The named command-level proof therefore passes while each finished story with unequal local and remote branch tips starts the `merge-base` call at `story.py:549`.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The cache assertion runs a second invocation of the same parameterized command, so it would pass if `next --json` used its own cache instead of the board's. The active-item proof at lines 90-97 counts only Git processes and never examines GitHub calls. Neither named proof detects a broken shared-cache contract or GitHub calls growing per active item; the existing GitHub call test covers `board` alone.
